elements.element: Restriction limited to a named competing product (no open-ended 'similar products/companies' sweep)
elements.evidence: "shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products" — the "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including... Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar...)" sweep is deleted

elements.element: Restriction operative during the term only
elements.evidence: "during the term of this Agreement"; added sentence: "shall apply during the term of this Agreement"
"and in any event for no longer than 12 months"
"shall not restrict the Company from internally developing web sites"
"or from continuing to operate any business or web site acquired by the Company"

elements.element: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer at all
elements.evidence: "the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products" remains operative

reasons: Locked target is the fallback and every fallback element is present: the restriction is narrowed to the defined Deerskin Products, limited to the term, capped at 12 months, and carved out for internal development and acquired businesses.

The replacement removes only the open-ended "substantially similar products/companies" sweep; the single inserted sentence is the shortest way to add the duration cap and the two carve-outs, which were wholly absent.

HDI's brand exclusivity for the term and the Section 6.2 closeout-merchandise retention are untouched; no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced ("Deerskin Products" and "term" are already defined/used).
Preferred (no restriction at all) is not achieved, which is expected at the locked fallback level and is not a deviation.
